comparison: Both evaluate claims C3, C20-C23 regarding in vivo pharmacology effects on synaptogenesis. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with adequate statistics and controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to systemic drug administration concerns - effects may be indirect through cortex/thalamus rather than specific to striatum. Major disagreement on interpretation.

Both evaluate claims C4, C26, C28-C30 on differential requirements for iSPNs vs dSPNs. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with adequate controls and statistics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting separate examination of D1R/A2aR antagonism and separation of dMSN/iMSN recordings rather than lumping conditions. Systemic administration concerns also apply.

Both evaluate claims C24-C25 on in vivo vs in vitro distinction. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, viewing negative in vitro result as evidence for circuit-level necessity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional slice experiments with cortex removed and ChR2 stimulation to definitively establish striatal specificity.

Both evaluate claims C5, C34, C36-C40, C42-C43 on glutamate uncaging experiments. Both agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes controlled glutamate design supports cell-autonomous mechanism. Peer Reviewer 2 states 'evidence for spinogenesis in slices is very strong' and provides 'strong evidence for role of corticostriatal activity and PKA signaling.' Strong concordance.

Both evaluate claims C44-C46, C48-C49 on pharmacogenetic PKA activation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights rigorous within-animal control design. Peer reviewers note optogenetic/chemogenetic experiments 'provide supporting evidence' and 'additional evidence for corticostriatal interaction,' with targeted viral transduction addressing some specificity concerns. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate claims C51-C56 on glutamate release sufficiency and PKA requirement. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with adequate controls and sample sizes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to systemic drug administration for blocking experiments, which 'could be reducing cortical activity through actions in cortex or thalamus.' Disagreement on pharmacological specificity.

Both evaluate claims C57-C59 (OpenEval includes C57, peer review focuses on C58-C59) on joint sufficiency of glutamate and PKA. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes ex vivo experiment directly tests cooperative mechanism. Peer reviewers state this addresses specificity concerns and would 'strengthen their hypothesis.' Strong concordance on reduced preparation evidence.

Both evaluate main conclusion claims C7, C60-C61 (peer review also includes C57). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by converging evidence demonstrating necessity and sufficiency. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 stating experiments 'do not establish that dopamine is critical for synaptogenesis' but only show 'D1R agonist can transiently bolster synaptic strength.' Major disagreement on strength of conclusions.

Both evaluate claims C17-C19 on anatomical characterization of dopamine innervation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes imaging data establishes developmental context. Peer reviewers note no concerns raised about these descriptive findings. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate claims C32-C33 on behavioral/locomotor effects. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with adequate statistics validating pharmacological manipulations are behaviorally relevant. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting 'transient effects' are demonstrated but 'never demonstrate these translate into long-term changes,' requesting follow-up experiments. Disagreement on interpretation of transient vs lasting effects.

Both evaluate claims C64-C66 on re-analyzed data from prior publication. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes re-analysis provides context for differential dSPN/iSPN effects. Peer reviewers note no concerns raised about these supporting findings. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate claims C1-C2, C8-C16, C27, C31, C35, C41, C62-C63, C68 representing established literature background. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these provide conceptual framework but are not novel findings. Peer reviewers note these background claims were not questioned. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate claims C67, C69 on broader implications and generalization. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation is reasonable but requires additional validation across systems. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, with editorial summary explicitly stating Reviewer 1 indicated such conclusions 'should be toned down throughout the manuscript.' Both skeptical but peer review more critical.

OpenEval evaluates claims C6, C50 on mechanistic explanation for differential iSPN requirements, finding SUPPORTED as inference from comparing in vivo and in vitro results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this mechanistic inference.

OpenEval evaluates claim C47 on developmental spine density changes, finding SUPPORTED with adequate statistics establishing developmental context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific developmental characterization.
